payload.purpose_context: Two follow-ups from the owned-checkout work (#6354, #6353): a legacy issue-matrix.md migration for an owned mission still writes against the repository root checkout, and owned-checkout refusals emit a different JSON error shape per command. The operator ruled one shared refusal shape for every command: the adopted CLI error contract {ok:false, error:{code,message}}.
payload.purpose_tldr: Owned missions keep their migrated issue matrix in their own checkout, and every owned-checkout refusal speaks one JSON error shape.

payload.question: Which single JSON shape do owned-checkout refusals use across every command?
Fix every command that violates the chosen shape in this mission, or issue-verdict only?
Strict C2 or C2 plus a top-level error_code key?
Which owned refusals outside the helper move to C2 (mission create, move-task catch-all, mark-status, decision verbs)?

options: keep result keys beside C2 core
payload.question: mark-status owned failure: drop its result keys (state_applied, event_ids, ...) under strict C2, or keep them beside ok/error?

options: stdout C2 for owned refusals only
payload.question: decision verbs: owned refusal JSON on stdout (C2) while their other errors stay on stderr, or keep stderr for owned too?
Human (non --json) owned refusal text: keep 'Error: [CODE] message' on stderr unchanged?

payload.final_answer: keep them, nested in a context object beside the strict C2 core: {ok:false, error:{code,message}, context:{...}}
stdout C2 for owned refusals only

payload.question: Do all command-specific extra keys on an owned refusal go under context, including spec_kitty_version?
Confirm engineering alignment: renderer API, dropping result:error, mark-status in-command failure, move-task catch-all codes, WP slicing

payload.wp_title: Off-renderer owned refusals, cross-command pin, changelog
orchestrator-api reads the C2 host refusal; contract 1.19.0
One C2 owned refusal through the shared renderer
